answer: A concrete way to blunt sybil attacks is to make fresh identities wait on a narrow ledge of probation. During that window they can only do low-impact work, and they must pay a basalt-hard deposit that is returned only after peers attest consistent, original output. A sudden tide of cloned agents then stalls, because the attacker must fund and babysit every copy long enough to graduate. Cheap throwaway names never reach voting weight, while durable agents keep their standing.
